city-digital-twin · Newcastle study · project report

Built to the footpaths, priced on a measured clock, and read by an instrument that lost its rail

2026-09-14HEAD 780c4c2branch maingate FAIL (1 of 19: board blocks - runs STALE, the running arm's iteration count; toolchain SKIPPED under the running arm; 17 PASS)

Ninth pass, read at 780c4c2 on main (the PR #195 merge, clean tree) two days after the previous one, and the first that follows a rebuild rather than a session: F34 put walk and bike on 40,203 footway ways and F35 made the taxi and ride engines route the trips they re-mode, and arm 0 of F35 - the first arm on the footpath network - was at iteration 287 of 300 when this was written, 28.7 h in, projected to land near 30 h against a 44 h ceiling approved on a 39.0 h quote. The scoreboard has not moved because nothing has been read: the only RESULT is still F32 at 0 of 12 inside 10 %, and its heavy-rail cell now reads 0 / -100 % on the board because the reader resolves a run's stops through the CITY's current schedule, which the rebuild overwrote, not the run's own - 22,487 of the result's 22,769 transit legs resolve to nothing, every doc gate is green, and the same run read +225 % three days ago. That is the sharpest of 7 defects, 31 risks and 27 smells at HEAD; the freight-train row is the same class (313 scheduled closures counted against a 405 target that includes the 92 freight closures the builder does emit). At arm 0's iteration-250 checkpoint - a citable reading, not a result - car is +9.3 % and motorbike -5.4 % (inside 10 % for the first time on any reading), bus moved from +44.8 % to -15.9 % and heavy rail from +225 % to +54 % when the pt access leg became physical, while bike went to +200 %, light rail to -73.5 % and ride stayed at -41.6 % against a coverage ceiling of 19.1 % that no constant can cross. Nineteen of the previous report's twenty recommendations were taken within 36 hours and none moved the goal count; the one not taken needs an external party (the TfNSW request, drafted twice, unsent). In the field, 53 projects and 12 platforms, the top validation rung (every simulated mode against its own ridership) is empty everywhere and this repository is the only attempt at it; the factor ledger reads IN 46 · PARTIAL 34 · INERT 3 · ASC 1 · OUT 10 over 94 rows, its top three movers (router-scorer consistency, headway and reliability, the rail bonus) all built and unrun. The iteration costs 347 s plain at 25 % on the footpath network (+42 % on F32), none of it this project's code; the 250-iteration horizon is reachable and arm 0 has executed it. The next thing to do is not another instrument: fix the reader, read arm 0 at its horizon, and spend the five paired arms in the decided order.

Method

Six agents, one per phase, launched together after the three collectors ran (collect_metrics.py twice - its gh call failed twice in a sandboxed background shell and succeeded in the foreground; collect_code_metrics.py; collect_performance.py), plus this session for Phases 0, 1, 8 and 9. Phase 2 read 86 files / 39,708 lines whole across six areas with a declared depth-of-read line per area (Areas 3-6 are ranked-subset reads; the signals stack and the 18 config groups were grep-scanned). Phase 3 read performance.json (190 runs, 36 timed), the running arm's own stopwatch.csv, gc.log and log head/tail, the Java listeners and the launcher. Phase 4 read all 71 PR blocks end to end, the commit log, timeline.json (305 dated events over 34 days) and the nine-report series with the two pruned reports recovered from git. Phase 5 read every living and archived document (DECISIONS.md only by its first 210 lines, headings, index and §14 log), every hook, workflow, skill and settings file, ran a relative-link check over 55 Markdown files and read all 124 issues. Phase 6 opened the reference library first and spent 40 of 40 calls over 6 rounds on its gaps, never-seen candidates and unknown cells (six PDFs read locally at no cost); Phase 7 spent 35 of 40 on the one layer-table row the library lacked and its gaps, and re-read all 94 statuses at HEAD by grep of the registry, the Java and the build layer with check_hardcoding.py --json as the INERT source. Phase 8 merged and deduplicated the findings, re-read 30 cited file:lines and re-fetched the six sources searched this pass (section §8.7 in the appendix), built the twelve-mode table from the board's reader on the result and on arm 0's it.250 checkpoint, the targets CSV, the registry and the thirteen position pages, and overrode one lane judgement with evidence. Ratings are 1-5 per dimension with two pieces of evidence each and are never averaged across areas.

Narrative

10 Aug: P0-P3 in one day - proposal, data package, network, demand - and by 11 Aug (PR #4) the run inputs load and a run costs 64 s/it at 25 %. 11-16 Aug: the registry (297 fields, config emitted), the cities/<city> split and the issue-32 network rebuild (PR #38, 73 commits); F1 completes the first 1000-iteration arms. 18-21 Aug: ride pairing built and found starved (#40), escort binding and age structure (#43), the first repaired-demand arm (34.7 h, #44), every mode made physical in a stranded stack (#46-#56), the two 67 h F4 arms; direct commits banned 21 Aug. 24-25 Aug: C5 exists and the project is renamed (#67), the ride collapse decomposed (#69), SUMO descoped (#79), the all-modes batch built inert (#80) and activated as F6 (#81); the first gate fires 25 Aug. 26-29 Aug: F7-F13 - the ride ratchet, joint travel, the pair re-found by the clock, taxi physical, SCATS as an algorithm, the yardsticks found contaminated and four conclusions corrected (#95, 40 commits). 30 Aug: the busiest day (87 commits, 31 record rows, seven families F14-F21), the demand rebuilt twice, licence rates measured, the documents restructured onto one page (#101). 31 Aug-2 Sep: fares priced (F22), bus first inside 10 % at a gate, the results store, three behaviour channels (F23), 25 % runs only. 3-6 Sep: every issue closed or awaiting a run and the issue gate (#111); the first whole-repository report and its 26 issues closed the same day (#138/#139); destinations balanced and the iteration halved (#140); a stopped run becomes citable (#143); F25 falsifies the demand cause for ride; a driver must own a car (#144). 7 Sep: four reports in one day (01:37 pruned, 13:02, 17:34, 23:17), car inside at the F28 gate (#146), the assessment's defects closed (#152/#153), the iteration decomposed to the method (#156). 8-9 Sep: the objective restated onto the twelve modes and the search made runnable (#166), F31's gate reads ride at the right length but too few (#161), four modes found decided in a layer with no controls (#170), the cost ceiling enforced (#171), and the first RESULT since F4: F32 relaxes and 0 of 12 are inside (#173). 10-11 Sep: the choice-set ceiling puts ride's target above its coverage (#176); the passenger is put on ride and every MATSim default declared (#177); F33 arm 0 launches (#178) and dies on a 14 GB heap (#179); the eighth report and the launcher that refuses what killed it (#193). 12-14 Sep: the report worked down, walk given a footpath network and pt access legs made physical (F34, #194, 243 files); the engines route what they re-mode (F35, #195); arm 0 launched 20:22 on a 39.0 h quote under a 44 h ceiling and at 14 Sep 01:22 stands at iteration 284 of 300, unread.

what_changed_since_20ae4e9
43 commits (PRs #180-#195), 275 files, +84,605/-5,838 lines. The run-side changes matter most: the launcher now refuses an overlay that changes nothing emitted and applies strict defaults (2b38233), procs.py unifies liveness and the store knows jvm_pid with a log-mtime grace (80ba4a1, b30c14b), preflight runs before detach, and completion boundaries are the result gate. In the Java, F35 (4a375f4) made the taxi and ride engines route the trips they re-mode through RemodeRestore, removing the whole-plan re-route of about 48,000 plans an iteration (24 % of CPU samples); the removal selector is injected into EscortCoherenceListener, GatedSubtourModeChoice treats an undecomposable plan as mixed, PtCrowdingScoring charges passengers still aboard at day end, installSingleton replaced seven pasted modules (#180), and the household roster's per-iteration re-map was measured at zero restores. The reading layer has one legs-table source per iteration and a per-process table cache (#182), the board skips failed runs and compare_runs is family-aware. Data: the TPA daily Opal patronage and BOAM series (#185, 434 records from a host outside the sandbox allowlist), BITRE registrations, preserved retrieval dates, a regenerated data dictionary, and the walk mode gained a footpath network (F34). The unit suite grew to 49 files / 323 functions but still imports 27 of 86 src modules. Family F35 is open and arm 20260912T202242_300it_25pct is running on it; nothing before it compares with anything after.
largest_simplification
Generate the 18 citysim ReflectiveConfigGroups (3,336 lines of @StringGetter/@StringSetter pairs shadowing declared registry fields) from config/schema/param_config.json and the registry's matsim_param bindings, so the Java parameter surface has one source and check_hardcoding's Java-shadow-default question becomes structural rather than textual; it removes 2,000-2,500 hand-written lines, touches no result (same names and defaults), and is guarded by dump_matsim_params.py diff and the existing 'group is registered on every stack' test pattern. Second, in Python: one Binder in build_activity_chains replacing the three 250-356-line passes (500-650 lines), guarded by a byte-diff of the committed WEEKDAY binding tables.

architecture
The build layer is a linear pipeline of module-level scripts, each anchored on src/city.py for paths and on src/registry for every declared value (CFG.get / CFG.sweep), writing regenerable artefacts that build_manifest.py hashes and lineage-tags. Since 20ae4e9 the legacy_symbol drift check is empty by design and check_hardcoding.py --strict is the only gate on values decided in a script; the layer's determinism rests on the seeded rng in build_population/build_activity_chains and on det_io. The demand half (activity chains 3,379 lines, plans 1,665) carries the model's structure - three binder passes, through/external tiers, per-day rewrite - in functions of 250-846 lines, and the run-input assembler re-reads the run network for each of five patch passes.

defectsrc/build/build_population.py332hs_vals = np.array([1,2,3,4,5,HH_TOP_BAND_MEAN]) puts B.population.household_size_top_band_mean at index 5, but :358 takes the geometric branch for bsz == 5 and only indexes hs_vals[bsz] for bsz 0-4, so the registry field (6.6, sweep 6.0-7.5, declared 12 Sep as 'used with the band midpoints') reaches no output.A sweep arm over household_size_top_band_mean is byte-identical to the base; the sweep ledger and check_hardcoding's unwired scan both see a CFG.get and report the field as consumed, so the sensitivity of household size to its top band is reported as zero when it was never tested.
risksrc/build/build_activity_chains.py637meandist.get(p, 8.0) (and P_INTERMEDIATE_STOP.get(purpose, 0.15) at :836/:979) are typed fallbacks in the framework demand builder that no registry field declares and that INLINE_ALLOW/ get-call structural exemptions hide from check_hardcoding.An HTS vintage that drops or renames a purpose row silently solves that purpose's distance decay to an 8.0 km target and its stop rate to 0.15, the diagnostic shows hts_network_km NaN, no message is printed and the chains build green.
risksrc/build/build_activity_chains.py980stop_purpose = 'HS' if u() < 0.5 else 'HO' decides the intermediate-stop purpose split with a typed 0.5 that is inside INLINE_ALLOW, so the gate cannot see a modelling value that is neither observed nor declared.The shopping/other split of intermediate stops is fixed at 50/50 for every city and every sweep; a reviewer reading the registry finds no field and concludes the split is measured.
risksrc/build/build_manifest.py698os.walk(base) iterates subdirectories in filesystem order (dirs is not sorted in place), so MANIFEST.csv row order depends on the OS and filesystem.A manifest regenerated on Linux CI or a second workstation differs from the committed one in row order only; check_manifest passes per row while the committed artefact's hash and the reproducibility claim ('regenerable byte for byte') do not hold.
risksrc/build/build_activity_chains.py2,531Through-traffic is seeded from calibration-split count rows only and the through share versus the external tier remains unreconciled (previous F5/F7 still open at HEAD).The holdout count stations receive no through seeding, so the holdout AADT error carries a structural deficit that the calibration stations do not, and the validation split measures a build asymmetry rather than model fit.
smellsrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py417if 'household_vehicles' in p.columns else None is a dead branch: the column is never in usecols, so the vehicles roster is always taken from the other path.A future reader assumes plans can carry the roster from the persons table; the branch never runs and the assumption is untestable.
smellsrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py1,438The first-day B2 CSV (about 323 MB) is streamed twice in main and again inside write_day; build_activity_chains.py reads each day file three times and rewrites it three times per day type (previous L11 open).The plans build spends most of its wall time re-parsing one file; a larger city or a 100 % sample makes the build I/O-bound before any modelling cost is reached.
smellsrc/build/build_matsim_network.py94JAVA_XMX = '-Xmx6g' and the worker/thread defaults at :723-725 are typed machine values in the framework while RUN.machine.xmx exists in the registry.A workstation with less than 6 GiB free fails pt2matsim with an opaque JVM error; a larger city needs a code edit rather than an overlay.
smellsrc/build/build_manifest.py766generated=datetime.datetime.now() is written into MANIFEST.json (one of 22 wall-clock sites in the build layers) and the limit parameter of sha256 (:122) is never used.Two regenerations of an unchanged package differ in MANIFEST.json, so a diff-based reproducibility check flags noise and a real change can hide behind it.
smellcities/newcastle/build/build_validation_targets.py119Date windows '2019-03-01'..'2020-03-01' and '2025-07-01' (:119-120, :163) and the literal 'Newcastle' at :426 are typed into the city builder where _city.target_lga() and a registry field would carry them.The vintage windows drift from the ones the position pages state and nobody can see it; the LGA filter breaks silently when the HTS release changes its area label casing.

testability
27 of 86 src modules are imported by a test and the demand half is not among them: build_activity_chains, build_matsim_plans and build_population have no unit test (code_metrics uncovered list), and their entry points are 178-846-line functions with module-level I/O at import (build_activity_chains.py:160, :2014; build_population.py:105-117), so a test must stand up a city on disk before it can call anything. build_matsim_network and build_matsim_run_inputs are covered only by smoke tests (test_module_smoke, test_score_msa_gate) and build_manifest by test_output_lineage; hts_purpose and asc_fields are the only build modules with behavioural tests. The pure helpers (shape_tools, gtfs_tools, det_io, osm_parse) are testable as they stand and untested.

architecture
run.py resolves registry + overlays + env + --set through src/registry, hands the resolved values to run_matsim.build_config, which emits the MATSim config, computes the run identity (controler_sha256, values_sha256, inputs_sha256), refuses an overlay that changes nothing emitted, runs preflight, and launches the pinned JVM directly or detached through Windows Task Scheduler. Three daemon threads (gate, ceiling, stall) watch the log and write a stop marker; completion is classified into ran_to_last_iteration / stopped_at_gate|ceiling|stall / stopped_by_operator and written to _run.json. results_store owns results/raw as a budgeted cache with _is_running (pid, jvm_pid, log-mtime grace) and extracts findings into results/processed via reporter subprocesses. Since 20ae4e9: procs.py unifies liveness, jvm_pid and the grace window landed, refuse_unrealised_overrides and the strict-default gate landed, preflight runs before detach.

defectrun.py137--list iterates run_matsim.RESULTS (the legacy results root) rather than results_store.run_names(); under the 9.137 store every run sits in results/raw or results/processed, so the listing prints the store's own subdirectories as 'incomplete'.An operator runs run.py --list to find a completed base for --resume, sees raw/processed/_launch marked incomplete and no run, and concludes nothing has completed.
defectsrc/setup/bootstrap_toolchain.py195RUN_STACK_POM (:195), JAVA_SRC and JAVA_SIGNALS_SRC (:255-256) are cwd-relative while TOOLS was anchored to the repo in the F28 fix, so the sources resolve only when the cwd is the repo root.--verify run from another directory prints 'no java sources under src/java' and then 'toolchain OK'; compile_java globs nothing and a stale .tools/classes is launched as if current.
defectsrc/setup/bootstrap_toolchain.py265'--force-compile' in sys.argv is the documented escape hatch for compiling under a running arm, but main()'s argparse (:473-479) declares only --verify and --run-stack and rejects the flag.An operator who must recompile while a smoke arm runs follows the docstring, argparse exits 2 with 'unrecognized arguments', and the only way through is to kill the arm; the unit test passes only because it monkeypatches sys.argv.
risksrc/run/run_matsim.py1,173reconcile_stale tests doc.get('pid') only, and run_failure.py:262 does the same, while results_store._is_running (:377) already knows both pid and jvm_pid.A harness killed by the OS while its JVM keeps writing (the #128 POSIX case, or a detached launcher whose parent died) has its directory renamed aborted_ under the live JVM; the JVM keeps writing into the renamed path and the run's record says it was aborted.
risksrc/run/prune_run.py61prune() has no running guard, is not routed through results_store (which 9.137 says is the only deleter), and the docstring at :5-9 claiming nothing in src/analyse reads ITERS is false (report_mode_ridership, iteration_trips read ITERS/it.N).A prune on a run still being read by the gate reporter removes the trips table between two milestones and the gate reads an empty iteration as a zero share.
risksrc/run/run_matsim.py715refuse_unrealised_overrides swallows every exception in the base-value emission (except Exception ... continue) and treats that key as realised.A derivation that raises for an unrelated reason (a missing overlay file, a schema change) makes the launcher accept an override that reaches nothing, which is exactly the silent no-op the check exists to refuse.
risksrc/run/results_store.py513trim calls process(name, extract=True) for every candidate even when _findings_in_processed(name) is already true, running two reporter subprocesses over every iteration on the launch-time daemon thread.A launch under a full cache spends its first minutes re-extracting already-extracted runs while the new JVM competes for the same cores; the stall watcher's grace window absorbs it today, a slower disk does not.
smellsrc/run/run_matsim.py2,043'-XX:+UseParallelGC', time.sleep(30) (:1501) and the 1800 s reporter timeout (:1516) are typed machine constants beside a registry that declares RUN.machine.*.A GC change or a longer reporter on a slower machine is a code edit and a DECISIONS entry nobody makes; the GC flag can move a result's wall time without appearing in the run identity.
smellsrc/run/session_gate.py123The local compile gate omits the cities tree while CI compiles it (test.yml compileall over src tests cities).A syntax error in a city builder passes /handoff and fails in CI after the PR opens.

testability
This is the best-tested area: run_matsim is imported by 12 unit tests (find_completed, ceiling, stall, stop, close-out, override-reaches-the-run, telemetry barrier), results_store by 5, and the tests use fixture stores rather than the real results/. The watcher threads are tested through log fixtures, which is the right seam; reconcile_stale is untested and holds the jvm_pid defect.

architecture
Everything that reads a run goes through report_mode_ridership.report(), which reads the iteration's trips/legs tables via iteration_reading's per-process cache, folds the twelve modes, scales boardings by 1/fraction and applies the gate bars from the registry; build_status_board, the gate watcher and calibrate's objective all call it. extract_metrics reads a stopped arm at reached_iteration and fit.py scores only calibration-split targets, marking unscorable ones. calibrate.py delegates run identity to run_matsim.find_completed and drives the arms as subprocesses; run_view/summarise_run scan the log incrementally. Since 20ae4e9 the reader has one source per iteration (the legs table), the board skips failed runs, compare_runs is family-aware and the table cache landed.

defectsrc/analyse/summarise_run.py383innovation_off_at = int(float(frac_off) * float(iterations)) (and run_view.py:318 int(float(frac_off) * target)) ignores firstIteration, while MATSim and EscortCoherenceListener.java:574 compute (last - first) * fraction + first.A warm-started arm (firstIteration 300, lastIteration 600, fraction 0.8) is judged 'relaxed' from iteration 480 while innovation is still on until 540; the relaxation verdict and the 'no plans created after the cutoff' basis are wrong for every resumed run.

architecture
The contract is the portable half (config/schema: field, registry, overlay, city, outputs, required_fields, matsim_defaults) and the resolver in src/registry that every consumer imports; each declared value must reach the emitted config (closure/reach probes) and every value decided in a script must appear in check_hardcoding's ledger, which is held at 0 by CI. Since 20ae4e9 CI also compiles cities, runs check_matsim_defaults --strict (F76 closed) and the strict-default refusal in the launcher; check_legacy_drift is empty and honest about it; check_city_agnostic proves a second city emits its own config. The registry holds 553 fields (assumed 203, definition 143, literature 81, derived 46, measured 42, observed 38; 466 with sweeps, 31 held_fixed, 42 derived_from, 136 matsim_param; 0 values outside their own sweep) and 172 fields with neither consumers nor matsim_param. The strongest checks are structural; the blind spots are semantic: a consumer that reads a field and drops it, a mode list typed in a reader, a typed value inside INLINE_ALLOW.

architecture
Acquisition is jurisdiction-specific by design: each adapter under cities/newcastle/extract fetches one source into data/raw (immutable) with a provenance_*.json, and the processed layers are derived from those by src/build with lineage recorded in MANIFEST.csv (lineage_scope, share_alike_ancestor from static OUTPUT_INPUTS declarations). The ODbL/CC-BY boundary is carried per row and the split is pre-registered in the validation targets. Since 20ae4e9: the TPA daily series (#185) and BITRE registrations arrived, retrieval dates are preserved across re-runs in fetch_open_data, the data dictionary was regenerated, and the truck target became calibration-only.

No adapter is imported by any test (code_metrics: 0 of 18), and most are module-level scripts that fetch on import, so they cannot be tested without a network or a refactor to functions; extract_daytype_factors and fetch_tpa_daily are the exceptions with a main(). The data artefacts are testable and tested mechanically (check_manifest in CI, check_package locally, the split asserted exactly), which is where the area's confidence comes from. A provenance-host allowlist test and a provenance-shape test would be cheap and are absent.

architecture
CitysimControler.assemble registers every citysim config group before the config is parsed (so an unmaterialised module fails consistency), loads the scenario, pins activities to usable links, and installs each extension conditionally on its representation field through installSingleton (#180). The engines act at sanctioned boundaries: RidePairingEngine and TaxiFleetEngine mutate selected plans at BeforeMobsim and restore at AfterMobsim through RemodeRestore; EscortCoherenceListener adds plans at ReplanningListener time through the injected removal selector; JointRideEngine, GenericRouteTeleporter and HouseholdCarDepartureHandler are qsim components in an explicit departure-handler order; the scoring handlers (crowding, fare, parking, bike stress, service quality) accumulate in handleEvent and emit deferred score/money events after mobsim. Unsynchronised handler state relies on eventsManager.synchronizeOnSimSteps, which RunTelemetry.requireSimStepBarrier asserts. Since 20ae4e9: the engines route what they re-mode (F35, 4a375f4), the removal selector is injected (F31 class), decomposition failure is treated as mixed (F63 closed), still-aboard passengers are charged (F58 class), and the roster's per-iteration re-map is measured at 0 restores.

risksrc/java/citysim/RidePairingEngine.java913ride.route.setTravelTime(driverTime + dwell) (:913, :1024) and the driver route rewrite (:1143-1152) mutate selected-plan routes from the routing worker threads submitted at :1212-1216, outside the single-threaded BeforeMobsim boundary the class documents.Two workers holding driver legs of one household write the same NetworkRoute; the mobsim reads a torn link list, an agent is inserted on a link its route does not contain and the run dies with a qsim assertion at a non-reproducible iteration.
risksrc/java/citysim/TaxiFleetEngine.java144sampleFraction = qsim().getFlowCapFactor() treats the flow capacity factor as the sample fraction; the registry derives RUN.sample.flow_capacity_factor from the fraction today, but the two are distinct fields and the fleet declared at full scale is sized by the wrong one if they ever diverge.A flow-capacity sensitivity arm (factor 0.5 at a 25 % sample) doubles the taxi fleet, the refusal rate halves and the taxi share moves for a reason nobody declared.
risksrc/java/citysim/JointRideEngine.java246vehicleOf builds Id.create(driver.toString()) and driver.toString() + "_" + car on every ride departure (the id-suffix convention read from the events), after the roster mapping lookup.MATSim changes the non-car vehicle suffix or the roster renames cars; the fallback silently resolves to a vehicle of another agent whose id happens to match and a passenger boards the wrong car (the comment says it degrades to a miss, but Id.create succeeds for any string).
risksrc/java/citysim/GatedSubtourModeChoice.java458if (after.size() != before.size()) return; skips every gate (reach, mixed-subtour, bound ride/drive, permissibility) whenever the stock module changes the trip count.A future MATSim release makes SubtourModeChoice insert or merge trips; every gate this class exists for is bypassed on those plans and the under-18 taxi leak the class was built for returns silently.
smellsrc/java/citysim/EscortCoherenceListener.java149The household map is filled at :718 and never read; boundDrivers(member) splits the attribute string for every member on every replanning (:275, :406, :593) while GatedModule caches the same parse by value (:167-184).Dead state and a per-replanning string parse over 155k persons; a cache miss is invisible in the profile because it is spread across every replanning.
smellsrc/java/citysim/RidePairingEngine.java701declared.contains(driver.person.toString()) allocates an id string per candidate pair in the pairing scan (java summary: 1 string-work site near a handler at FareChargeHandler:91, 2 Id concatenations in ScatsPriorityProbe:165,186).The pairing scan's cost scales with candidates x households in allocations rather than comparisons; on a 100 % sample the BeforeMobsim pass becomes the iteration's longest single-threaded stretch.
smellsrc/java/citysim/RunTelemetry.java314openByVehicle and loadByLink arrays are reallocated on every reset (:314, :316), the freeflow map boxes a Double per link (:146) and each frame copies two TreeMaps (:251-252).Per-iteration garbage of two arrays sized by the id count plus per-frame map copies; with -Xmx pinned by RUN.machine.xmx a longer horizon spends more of each iteration in GC than the telemetry's own accounting shows.
smellsrc/java/citysim/CitysimControler.java24719 config groups are registered by hand into a fixed-index array (new ConfigGroup[19 + extraGroups.size()], :247-270); the seven pasted modules are gone (installSingleton, #180) but assemble is still 579 lines.The twentieth group is added to the list of constructors and not to the count, the array is one short and MATSim fails at the consistency check with 'Unmaterialized config group' for whichever group lost its slot.
smellsrc/java/citysim/HouseholdVehicleRoster.java122Integer.parseInt(n.toString()) on the householdVehicles attribute has no guard, and :151 allocates a new HashMap per driver per iteration.A plans file with 'NA' in one household's attribute kills the run at iteration 0 with a NumberFormatException naming no person.
smellsrc/java/citysim/RemodeRestore.java197route() creates and shuts down a fixed thread pool on every call, once per engine per iteration.Two pools of global.numberOfThreads threads are created and torn down per iteration; harmless today, but the pattern invites a third engine to do the same.

testability
The Java has no unit test harness; behaviour is probed by the six main()-bearing probe classes (GatedSubtourProbe, RemodeRestoreProbe, NestedSubtourProbe, GradientTableProbe, PtFareProbe, SubtourChainScan) run by hand, and by Python tests that read the Java source as text (test_raptor_mode_cost, test_service_quality, test_telemetry_barrier, test_plan_removal_one_selector, test_direct_walk_counters). The engines are testable in principle - RemodeRestore, PtCrowdingScoring and TaxiFleetEngine take a Scenario and an EventsManager and have no static state - but nothing exercises them off a full run, so a threading defect like RidePairingEngine:913 can only appear as a dead arm. A JUnit target compiled against the pinned jar with synthetic 100-person scenarios is the missing seam.

beforeMobsimListeners
classes
citysim.RidePairingEngine (BeforeMobsim+AfterMobsim+PersonDeparture handler, RidePairingEngine.java:131,497) and citysim.TaxiFleetEngine (BeforeMobsim+AfterMobsim, TaxiFleetEngine.java:103,198); MATSim's own PlansDumping ('dump all plans') runs in the same phase
TaxiFleetEngine.notifyBeforeMobsim
collect() walks every selected plan for taxi legs, sorts the requests, simulates the fleet queue (fleet 200 = 800 x 0.25) and calls remodeRefused(): RemodeRestore.route() builds a NEW Executors.newFixedThreadPool(20) and ONE TripRouter per worker (routers.get() at RemodeRestore.java:203) every iteration that has a refusal, routes each refused trip as a network walk, inserts it in refusal order; restore after the mobsim. Measured on the arm: 47,555 ms for 45,573 refusals at it.0, 2,158 ms for 2,150 at it.283 - the cost follows the refusal count
RidePairingEngine.notifyBeforeMobsim
index() is hoisted already (guarded by indexed, RidePairingEngine.java:1594-1633); per iteration it allocates current = new HashMap<>() and clears ten maps/counters, walks every selected plan of 155,233 persons in id order (ordered), pairs, routes driver detours on global.numberOfThreads workers (one TripRouter each), re-times 60,431-60,437 declared passengers, and re-modes the 272-644 unpaired ride legs through the same RemodeRestore.route(); ride_pairing elapsed_ms ~1 s since §9.147
what_is_hoistable
the fixed thread pool and the per-worker TripRouters in RemodeRestore.route() (rebuilt every call, twice an iteration - taxi and ride); the ordered person list and index() already are. TaxiFleetEngine's PriorityQueue of fleet double[2] entries is trivially small
what_allocates
RemodeRestore: a Remode job per refused trip (2,150-48,200) holding the ORIGINAL plan elements for the restore; the routed walk legs and their NetworkRoute link lists (plan memory - these are the bytes plans.xml.gz grew by, 751 -> 902-931 MB gz per dump against the F33 probe); RidePairingEngine: current HashMap of realised times, detours LinkedHashMap, rides ArrayList
measured_share
beforeMobsimListeners 17 s median of 347 (4.9 %) on the arm, 46 s at it.2-24, 15 s in the tail; on the probe 70.5 s (15.2 %) because 81 % of taxi requests were refused there
iterationStartsListeners
citysim.HouseholdVehicleRoster (re-maps every person's car vehicle id, 155k persons, 'well under a second', HouseholdVehicleRoster.java:72-112) and citysim.RunTelemetry.reset() (RunTelemetry.java:293-320: clears seven maps and REALLOCATES openByVehicle = new LinkEntry[Id.getNumberOfIds(Vehicle)+1024] and loadByLink = new LinkLoad[Id.getNumberOfIds(Link)+1024] every iteration - the hoist the 11 Sep pass ranked 11th, not taken); phase reads 0 s at 1 s resolution on every run
replanning
citysim.EscortCoherenceListener.notifyReplanning (index() then a scan of every household car leg; proposes nothing past the cutoff, §9.158) inside MATSim's own strategy pass - not separable on the stopwatch
afterMobsimListeners
RidePairingEngine/TaxiFleetEngine restore the original trips; BikeStressScoring, PtCrowdingScoring, ParkingChargeHandler, PtFareChargeHandler, FareChargeHandler emit deferred score/money events; phase reads 0 s
iterationEndsListeners
RunTelemetry.publishIterationEnd() appends one telemetry.jsonl line (2.4 MB after 283 iterations) and rewrites telemetry_links.json (2.8 MB); MATSim's experienced-plans writer on checkpoint iterations (47-83 s); 1-2 s otherwise
startup_only
citysim.SharedModeNetworks (one routing network per distinct link set, 4 for 7 modes, §9.167)

mobsim

host
Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, 24 cores / 24 logical (Get-CimInstance), 63.46 GB RAM; performance.json host_cpu_count 24
threads_in_force
qsim numberOfThreads 16 (RUN.machine.threads; config.xml:42), global.numberOfThreads 20 (RUN.machine.replanning_threads; also the re-mode and detour routing pools), SimStepParallelEventsManager 4 threads (RUN.machine.event_handler_threads; matsim.log:256), synchronizeOnSimSteps true, oneThreadPerHandler false
average_parallelism_measured
JVM CPU 912,109 s over 103,571 s uptime (Get-Process CPU / gc.log uptime) = 8.8 cores busy on average, 37 % of the 24 - the mobsim's 16 threads are barrier-bound and every other phase is 1-20 threads; §9.147 measured 10 -> 24 qsim threads buying 8 %, so the idle cores are not buyable, and a second arm does not fit (JVM peak working set 52.5 GB of 63.5; #66 one-arm rule)
qsim_settings
linkDynamics PassingQ, trafficDynamics queue, usingFastCapacityUpdate false (the signals contrib refuses true, §9.142), timeVariantNetwork true (2,441 change events on 16 links, all 368k links pay the binarySearch - §9.155's bounded lever, not done), vehicleBehavior teleport, stuckTime 10 s, removeStuckVehicles false, snapshotperiod 00:00:00, start 0 h end 30 h, main modes car/truck/motorbike/walk/bike/taxi, flowCapacityFactor = storageCapacityFactor = 0.25
pt_vehicles
2,139 transit departures a day over 1,270 routes / 261 lines (cities/newcastle/scenarios/matsim/S2/WEEKDAY/transitSchedule.xml.gz, the file config.xml names); seats scaled x0.25 with floor 1 (44->11, 60->15, 98->24, 149->37; _meta.json sample.transit_capacity_scaled); per-iteration pt-vehicle count is not in telemetry.jsonl (it carries person departures by legMode: bus 9,536, rail 3,128, ferry 324, tram 196 at it.282)
stuck_agents_per_iteration
F35 arm median 4,442.5 (telemetry.jsonl, 282 iterations); it.282: 2,274 (walk 1,662, bus 285, car 124, rail 60, ride 62); F32 arm median 5,031; probes 21,115-23,922 (a probe's first iterations, not comparable)
departures_per_wall_second
F35 arm median 8,007.8 (2,798,347 departures / iteration), F32 arm 2,555.2 (623,176) - NOT a speed-up: 2.31 M of the F35 departures are walk legs (1,115,673 network walk + 1,188,501 non_network_walk at it.282) the road-graph arm never executed as legs (accessEgressModeToLink, RUN.transit_router.access_egress_basis network)
pace_vs_fraction
the sampling page states no pace law - it says never compare across fractions and that 1 % is unusable for results. Measured on ONE stack (F35): 1 % 49.5 s (8 threads) vs 25 % 460.0 s probe / 347 s arm = 7.0-9.3x for 25x the agents - strongly sublinear, because the 2,139 pt runs, the 368k-link graph, the SpeedyALT landmarks and the per-iteration fixed passes are paid at any fraction; mobsim 34.5 -> 262 s (7.6x), replanning 9 -> 130 s (14x). Across the only same-build 10 %/25 % pair (F1: 33.34 vs 90.19 s) it is 2.7x for 2.5x, i.e. linear above 10 %. The rebuild's cost ALSO scaled with agents x graph: +35 % at 1 %, +88-127 % at 25 % (§9.168)

replanning

strategy_weights
ChangeExpBeta 0.7, ReRoute 0.15, SubtourModeChoice 0.1 (person subpopulation only), TimeAllocationMutator 0.05 (external and freight: ChangeExpBeta/ReRoute/TimeAllocationMutator; config.xml:180-227; RUN.replanning.weights, literature, proportional sweep 0.5)
innovation_off
fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation 0.8 -> cutoff at iteration 240 of 300 (_progress.json innovation_off_at 240); the tail is 60 of 301 iterations = 20 %
plan_memory
maxAgentPlanMemorySize 8 (literature, sweep [3, 10]); removal WorstPlanSelector; no score MSA (absent)
router_calls_per_iteration
on 155,233 persons: ReRoute ~23,300 whole plans (0.15) + SubtourModeChoice ~15,500 plans re-routed on the changed subtour (0.10) + TimeAllocationMutator ~7,800 (0.05, no re-route in the strategy name) ~ 39,000-46,000 plan routings inside replanning (20 threads), PLUS on our side 2,150-48,200 refused-taxi walks and 272-644 unpaired rides (beforeMobsimListeners) and the driver detours; PersonPrepareForSim now re-routes nothing (2 s for 155,233 persons, matsim.log 01:08:01-01:08:05). Verdict on the 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon is reachable at the measured pace and arm 0 has already executed it: iterations 0-249 took 25.6 h of iteration wall on the footpath network (~26 h with setup), the whole 300 will land near 30 h against a 44 h ceiling and a 39.0 h quote, and the run has been relaxed since the cutoff (max drift 0.11 pp). The pace itself is the honest news: a plain 25 % iteration is 347 s, +42 % on the F32 road-graph arm's 243.5 s, and none of it is ours - the mobsim is 236 s (68 %) moving 2.8 M departures of which 2.3 M are walk legs the road graph never executed, replanning 85 s (24.5 %) is MATSim's router on 2.1x the links, and this project's own listeners are 17 s (4.9 %) and falling with the taxi refusal count; the F35 Java change took the 92 s PersonPrepareForSim re-route to 2 s and is the only per-iteration repair since 11 Sep, measured probe-to-probe at -17 %. The heap is not binding (live set plateaus at 25-29 GB under 48g, GC 2.45 % of wall), the log is 13.6 MB not 51 GiB, and the three zero-per-iteration refusals the last pass asked for (heap rule, stall kill, checkpoints) are in the launcher and have cost nothing yet because nothing has died. Nothing on the table halves the iteration: threads are saturated (8.8 of 24 cores busy on average and 24 threads bought 1 %), the events knob is bracketed, FIFO and teleported walk are refused on correctness, and the two largest unmeasured levers (a plain-link factory for the 368k time-invariant links, a footpath-graph contraction for the router) are network changes that each need a probe arm before they can be priced. What the measurements DO buy is 5-7 h per arm at zero model cost - a horizon declared at 250 (3.8-4.6 h, a decision), checkpoints every 50 (0.4 h), and quoting arms on an arm's own banded clock so a 30 h arm stops occupying a 44 h approval.

what the comparison says

  • Fifty-three comparable projects and twelve platforms; the top rung (every simulated mode scored against its own ridership) is empty across all of them, and this repository's attempt at it reads 0 of 12 inside 10 % at its newest result, with arm 0 of F35 running and unread.
  • Smartcard-validated agent-based models exist (Cape Town R2 0.85 on AFC boardings; Seoul station volumes) but one operator at a time; this city's Opal per-mode datasets are on the hub and no comparable project scores several transit modes on tap data at once.
  • No agent-based project has measured whether signals move a validation figure: the Berlin signals application ran one iteration to check connectivity, and Barcelona held a generic actuated controller fixed at 2,035 signals while moving R2 to 0.81 by assignment. SCATS-as-published-algorithm is above the whole field's fidelity floor with no comparator.
  • The field's count fits sit at two operating points - full demand (Barcelona, 2.06 M trips, 30 h a run) or calibrated capacity (MATSim-NYC, factor 0.15 at 4 %) - and a 25 % sample with capacity scaled 0.25 is neither; the repaired station map (+16.3 % mean, -1.1 % median, 0 zeros) is the project's own first reading at that point.
  • The 25 % directive now has a published basis: Mersini & Ziemke 2026 finds 1 % and 5 % unreliable and 10 % 'substantially more reliable', with sample selection dominating the seed - which is the definition of the replication band the objective still divides by zero.
  • The one non-myopic simultaneous calibration in the literature (Chen 2020) ran on a 351,518-person prototype city, needed an analytical logit gradient MATSim does not have, never reported a wall time, and could not move its mode-choice component - so the field offers no affordable multi-target architecture this project has not already declined.
  • Trip-length distributions are calibrated jointly with modal split in one read case (mobiTopp Stuttgart), by eye, with purpose-specific destination scaling; the matsim-scenarios READMEs name the same target without a method. This project's geometry deficit on five modes has no published numeric protocol to borrow.
  • Two agent-based engines on one demand and one mode-choice model disagree by up to 2.4 pp (car) and 4.3 vs 3.2 % (ride): a 10 % band on a sub-1 % mode is inside the cross-engine band, and the field has no published acceptance bar for mode choice at all.

data acquired answer

Across the rows that state their acquisition, comparable projects validate cars on agency-held or open count stations (Barcelona 488 city stations as AADT; MWCOG 7,889 directional links; MATSim-NYC 46 of 597 NYC DOT locations; AToM 87 VicRoads segments), transit on operator boardings (MWCOG, SoundCast by operator, Munich stop-level MVV, MATSim-NYC turnstile entries) and - new this pass - on smartcard transactions for a single operator (Cape Town MyCiTi AFC; Seoul T-money), active modes almost nowhere (AToM's 48 + 48 sensors are the only counters in 53 rows), taxi and rideshare nowhere as counts, and freight only as classified counts or auxiliary models. This package holds RMS permanent hourly counts (30 calibration stations plus holdout, classified heavy-vehicle shares at 24), Opal station entries and per-mode trip datasets from the TfNSW hub, NSW HTS aggregates, the census journey-to-work and G62 tables, TfNSW signal locations, BITRE fleet counts by postal area, and - since 12 September - a bounded ferry observation (234-1,347 weekday tap-ons at the Newcastle wharf) that no other Australian row has; it lacks what the whole field lacks (bike and pedestrian counters, taxi trip records) and one thing the field has that it does not use yet: tap data scored per mode, which the Cape Town row shows is workable at R2 0.85 with the data's own defects stated.

physical fidelity answer

In the field, active modes are teleported (Berlin v5 walk 4 km/h beeline, bike 12 km/h; every ActivitySim agency row has no mobsim at all; mobiTopp is zone-based) and only AToM and this project route them on a network; public transport is schedule-based on the network in the MATSim rows and matrix-assigned in the agency rows; adaptive signals appear in no base case (Berlin: 'traffic lights are typically not modeled explicitly'; MATSim-NYC folds signals into free speeds and capacity; POLARIS carries 'an early switch to green' only as a lever; Barcelona substituted SUMO's generic actuated controller for the city's unavailable plans and held it fixed; Ziemke & Braun's Berlin signals ran one iteration to check connectivity). This project runs walk and bike physically on a footpath network built 12 September (363,818 walk links, pt access and transfer walks as network legs, teleported = 0 on the probes), four pt modes on the mapped GTFS, SCATS as its published algorithm with transit signal priority, priced parking with search time, and freight rail as timetable-derived level-crossing closures. The honest comparison is unchanged and sharper: nobody in the field has shown that any of that detail moves a validation figure, the one stored case of fidelity reaching a figure is Berlin v6's SUMO-calibrated free speeds, and this project's own paired-arm design for measuring it (#172) cannot start until arm 0 of F35 - the control half of all five pairs - has read.

warm start answer

No surveyed row describes warm-starting a calibration from a prior run's plans as a method; the nearest practices are the matsim-scenarios habit of shipping calibrated output plans as the next release's input plans (Berlin, Kelheim, Lausitz - stated in READMEs without a claim about what it saves), mobiTopp's calibration rounds that reuse the previous round's assignment travel-time matrices, and the MATSim platform's own restart answer (issue #834: resume AT a checkpoint iteration from its post-replanning plans, losing everything since the last dump). This project's --warm-start is that platform mechanism with two additions: it re-derives the innovation cutoff so the restarted arm's cutoff iteration is the parent's (#192), and arm 0 of F35 dumps plans every 25 iterations so a death like F33's at iteration 98 (checkpoints at 0 and 1 only, 6.5 h lost) cannot recur. What a warm start is WORTH in hours is stated by nobody, here or in the field: it is crash recovery, not a bit-identical continuation, and whether a warm-completed arm counts as an arm remains a project ruling (#75). Unknown everywhere else.

calibration_method
family
coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (unchanged, never run to completion) PLUS, NEW AT THIS HEAD AND NEVER RUN, an implemented ASC log-ratio fixed point - src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py. Read from the source at HEAD 781cf41, not searched.
what_the_source_says
src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 runs coordinate descent: per round, per free parameter, per grid point across that parameter's registry sweep, a FULL MATSim run -> extract_metrics -> fit -> a weighted scalar objective over declared _fit.json components, keeping a point only if it is feasible against the C4 occupancy and trip-length constraints; the round stops when the improvement falls below delta. The search space is DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY, not listed in the script: a field is free only if it is source=assumed, carries a scalar sweep and is not held_fixed. The six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore unreachable from the loop by construction - so this project has NO log(target/modelled) ASC loop of any kind. The one constant that is solved, asc_car_passenger, is solved in a separate module (solve_asc_ride.py:101-121) by SECANT INTERPOLATION ON log(ride_per_car) against the observed passenger:driver ratio, and is reported as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The loop refuses to fit more parameters than the objective identifies (four independent numbers) and cannot read a holdout row by construction.
objective_evaluations
coordinate descent: calibrate.py:433 computes the budget as sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs; at 25% an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall, so a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round search is ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours. THE LOOP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN TO COMPLETION. The ASC fixed point is far cheaper by design - TWO arms settle the contraction question - and is the only one of the two that has an evaluation count small enough to state in advance. Neither has been executed.
convergence_criterion
round-over-round objective improvement < delta

asc_fixed_point_new_this_pass
src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py EXISTS and PROPOSES ONLY; it has NEVER BEEN RUN. It applies delta_i = damping * [ ln(target_i/modelled_i) - ln(target_ref/modelled_ref) ] against car as reference - the same object as the Berry (1994) share inversion and the same expression matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes verbatim, with the damping declared on CAL.asc.damping. THREE DESIGN CHOICES ARE UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE TEST IS THE CONTRACTION, NOT THE SHARES - two damped rounds are compared mode by mode, and if |delta| shrinks the residual is a taste that constants will close, while if it does not shrink the deficit is STRUCTURAL and no constant will ever close it. That is a cheap, decisive, published-in-spirit answer to the 'constant or mechanism' question that the agency protocol answers only by ordering. (2) It CANNOT REACH A FROZEN CONSTANT: it reads held_fixed from the registry and refuses, structurally, the way the holdout guard refuses. (3) On heavy rail and light rail the step is marked basis_is_boardings and reported as a PROXY, because the logit inversion is exact only for shares of a common total. ROUND 1 IS PROPOSED OFF THE F31 GATE AND NOT APPLIED: bike -0.5121, bus -0.2301, ferry +0.6713, light rail +0.4143.
read_against_the_field_this_pass
Two published methods now bracket this project's loop and both were read this pass. (1) Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva (2020, TR-C 119:102650) names this project's coordinate descent for what it is: 'myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters' - and their non-myopic alternative calibrates precisely this project's target set at once (activity shares, mode shares, mode-specific OD flows, mode-specific sensor counts). (2) The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim framework publishes New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion) verbatim - the exact expression in asc_fixed_point.py - inside a CYCLIC protocol over model components, and states plainly that 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously.' | 2026-09-11 (third bracket): POLARIS's published procedure is the same cyclic ASC-by-purpose update, TIERED by iteration so that 'network state' can 'adapt to this change in demand' before the next tier is touched, with counts and speeds explicitly outside the calibrated set ('can only be minimally calibrated'). MATSim-NYC calibrated NO demand constants at all - its nested logit was estimated on RHTS + TLC/FHV/Citi Bike records and converted analytically - and spent its six SPSA iterations on twelve link-CAPACITY factors instead, which is the opposite allocation to this project's.

status
from the registry and position pages at HEAD 780c4c2
signals
SCATS implemented as its published algorithm (A.signals.scats.*: target degree of saturation, cycle bounds, DS smoothing/deadband, cycle step) + transit signal priority (A.signals.tsp.*); the offset library is swept because it is not published
pt_dwell_priority
bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry run the mapped GTFS on the mapped network; TSP declared; PT access, egress and transfer walk legs are NETWORK LEGS the qsim executes since 12 September (#167 closed on the 1 % probes, teleported=0); MATSim's coordinate-to-link stubs remain (median 54 m)
parking
priced parking with search time (A.parking.*: charged hours, modes, price percentiles, search time); no parking-supply occupancy layer (the hub's Park&Ride 'Car park API' is not held)
level_crossings
freight rail represented as timetable-derived level-crossing closures (314 movements)
did_fidelity_move_a_validation_figure
not yet measurable - no paired arm with a fidelity control has closed; arm 0 of F35 (running) is the CONTROL half of all five pairs (#172), so the first such measurement is at least two arms away
warm_start
--warm-start <dead run dir> exists in src/run/run_matsim.py: it resumes from a dead run's newest plans checkpoint, records warm_started_from, and RE-DERIVES RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation so the innovation cutoff ITERATION is the parent's (the pinned jar's first + f x (last - first) had moved it 240 -> 260 at N = 100, #192). It is crash recovery, not a bit-identical continuation. Arm 0 of F35 dumps plans every 25 iterations for exactly this reason (the F33 arm that died at 98 had checkpoints at it.0 and it.1 only). This matches the platform's own answer (MATSim issue #834: restart AT the checkpoint iteration from its post-replanning plans); the platform has no finer mechanism, and the interval is the whole trade. No surveyed row states a warm start from a prior calibrated run except as the matsim-scenarios practice of shipping calibrated output plans as input plans.

signals_addendum_2026_09_14
Ziemke & Braun 2021 (Procedia CS 184:745-752, doi 10.1016/j.procs.2021.03.093; VSP WP 20-40 read in full): OSM-derived signals and lanes were added to the Open Berlin Scenario and 'one iteration of the co-evolutionary algorithm was run to verify that the automated generation of signal and lane data results in a connected and correct network' - the 'verification' is structural, not against counts or travel times. Default fixed-time plans from German guidelines (90 s cycle, 10 s minimum green, 5 s all-red; extra green by lane count): 'This signal plans do not necessarily model a realistic signal control.' 'As the simulation of traffic signals and lanes in MATSim significantly increases runtime, the automated generation tool provides a possibility to ...' restrict the signalised area; 'only MATSim's Dijkstra implementation works with lanes, which is comparably slow.' Whether signals move a count fit in Berlin remains UNMEASURED in the published record.

Platforms (12)
  • name
    MATSim (Multi-Agent Transport Simulation)
    engine
    Java; co-evolutionary iterative agent-based simulation - demand, mobsim (queue-based traffic flow), replanning, iteration control, analysis, all modular and replaceable
    licence
    GNU General Public License - declared in the <licenses> block of matsim/pom.xml on master: name 'GNU General Public License', url ${basedir}/COPYING, comments 'See also the LICENSE file'. Note that GitHub's own licence API returns 404 for the repository (no SPDX-detectable LICENSE at the root), which is why four earlier fetch routes found nothing; scenario repositories built on it record GPL-2.0 for their own code. CLOSED this pass.
    last_release
    MATSim 2026 (Spring), released 10 April 2026; annual April cadence since 2020 (2025 Spring 11 Apr 2025, 2024 Spring 13 Apr 2024)
    city_agnostic
    yes by design - a toolbox, not a city model; every city is a scenario built on it
    does_best
    The reference open engine for large-scale agent-based transport simulation: a replaceable-component architecture in which route, mode, departure time and plan memory are all co-evolved to a stochastic user equilibrium
    who_runs_on_it
    Berlin, Leipzig, Kelheim, Lausitz, Metropole Ruhr, Duesseldorf, Dresden, Hannover, Kyoto, Mexico City, Santiago de Chile, Gauteng, New York City (NYU C2SMART), Vienna (AIT), Melbourne (AToM), Tyne and Wear (Newcastle University), Dhaka, Brussels, Infrastructure Victoria MABM, Wellington NZ (in build) - all from this library's project rows

    calibration_tooling
    Three named routes, all read this pass: (1) matsim.calibration in matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools - an ASCCalibrator driving an Optuna study, whose update is literally log(z_i) - log(m_i) - (log(z_0) - log(m_0)), i.e. the classic ASC fixed-point loop normalised on a fixed reference mode, with a pluggable learning-rate scheduler and a TerminationCondition dataclass whose check_termination carries "# TODO: not used yet"; (2) Cadyts, a Bayesian count calibration that adjusts NO parameter and instead adds a utility bonus so agents select the plans matching observed counts; (3) opdyts (Flotterod, TR-B 2017), which approximates point equilibria of the mobsim/scoring/replanning loop, with a Berlin mode-constant example. See calibration_methods.
    carried_to
    2026-09-14
    restart_mechanism
    NO checkpoint/resume exists in the platform. The developer answer (Marcel Rieser, matsim-code-examples issue #834, 12 Dec 2022, read via api.github.com this pass): 'The plans in "it200/200.plans.xml.gz" are the plans after replanning, but before mobsim, in iteration 200. So you can use those to resume at iteration 200 (it should generate the same events file like the first run), and then continue with iteration 201.' and 'If you use the plans file of iteration 200, start the new run also with iteration 200.' ... 'The first iteration of a run never does replanning.' So a resume is a plans-file restart AT the checkpoint iteration, and only where a plans dump exists (writePlansInterval); everything since the last dump is lost. Memory rule of thumb from the same repository's issue #189: 'typically... around 100KB per agent. That is 1 GB per 10k agents' (mrieser, 2019-08-20); a ~1M-agent, 250k-link scenario needed 60-90 GB actual (mrieser); JVM total is ~25% above the reported heap (josiekre).

A1AResidential location (fixed from census)INB1 fixes residence from the census: src/build/build_population.py fits per SA1 to G34/G35/G36/G04/G43/G46/G17/G60 and jitters the home inside the SA1 at B.population.home_jitter_radius_factor (declared b1ee98c; build_population.py:40, :350). Never re-chosen in a run.Nothing on the current board; residence is where the observation puts it.Residential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the built-environment effect and mis-states only the self-selected minority.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S02642751210018522026-09-07
A2AWorkplace locationPARTIALWorkplaces are placed by a solved gravity on the census place-of-work attractor (D.attraction.job_weight_by_category, src/build/build_zone_attractions.py:64; D.attraction.education_population_floor :25) with the HW mean distance solved per home LGA (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:499 calibrate_decay) and destination-end constraints (B.activity.destination_balancing, :295). No OD-pair journey-to-work flow is scored against the census W-tables; no shadow price.pt mean trip 10.96 km against 23.4 observed - a work OD check would say whether the long pt commute exists in the demand at all (heavy_rail +225.0, light_rail -58.6). MWCOG Gen3 validates county-to-county JTW flows with a 10 % rule (this pass).Workplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2112.120712026-09-08

C1CAttraction by purpose (jobs, floorspace, enrolments)INAttraction by purpose from census place-of-work employment, POIs and CBD building footprints (data/processed/landuse/D1_zone_attractions_SA1.csv; build_zone_attractions.py:64 JOB_WEIGHT, :25 EDU_POP_FLOOR; build_activity_chains.py:450 load_poi_by_zone); D.landuse.poi_attraction_weights and D.landuse.retail_gfa_share 0.35 declared at b1ee98c (cities/newcastle/build/build_landuse_parking.py:40-41), formerly inline literals.light_rail -58.6: the corridor's shopping ends reach 0.99x their attraction share since 9.142; the tram still has to be chosen.The practice is settled on size terms: each destination alternative's utility is a set of impedance terms plus one size function, where the size term is total or industry-specific employment for work, school enrolment for education, and for non-work purposes only the relevant categories - retail employment for shopping, restaurant employment for meals - with households or population for social purposes. C2CDistance decayINGravity decay solved per purpose x home LGA so the expected NETWORK distance equals the HTS mean through the measured detour factor (build_activity_chains.py:499 calibrate_decay); short kernel B.activity.short_trip_mean_km at B.activity.short_trip_band_share (:285-287).walk -26.5: the published HTS gives a mean and no distribution, so the short end's SHAPE is unobserved (9.164); the bespoke trip-length-by-mode table is drafted, not sent (J7).The gravity/spatial-interaction relationship declines with distance, time and cost; the two competing deterrence forms are the power law and the negative exponential, with the negative exponential generally the preferred form in transport application, and the estimated deterrence parameter is sensitive to the spatial arrangement of the study area.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S09600779150015872026-09-07

E6ECar availability and competition for household carsINCar availability = licence AND household vehicle (AvailabilityModesCalculator bound at CitysimControler.java:303; RUN.mode_choice.consider_car_availability true); competition for the household's cars is physical (B.population.vehicle_roster census; HouseholdVehicleRoster :483; HouseholdCarDepartureHandler :527-528).car +11.3 / ride -41.0: 10,224 of 20,902 declared escort pairs had the passenger driving their own car at it.300; every_plan placement is the demand-side remedy and F35 arm 0 is its first reading.Car availability is the binding constraint on mode, not a preference: the elasticity of active-mode use with respect to car ownership is about -2.6, and the resource logic is that a chain-based mode can only be used if the vehicle is where the traveller left it. No age or sex coefficient in scoring; the MODELLED mode x age table exists (mode_by_demographics.py) and the observed one is one bespoke table away - the request is drafted, not sent (docs/requests/tfnsw_hts_bespoke_tables.md, b8f6577).bike +113.0: 12-17 year olds cycle 15.4 % of their trips in the model; the observed mode x age cell is the blocked acquisition (#50).Age and sex segment travel with a transferable magnitude on the ACTIVE modes. Across 19 major cities in 13 countries and 6 continents (8 low-and-middle-income, 11 high-income), females are more likely than males to walk in every city - on average 23% more likely - and on average 6% more likely to use public transport, while the relation REVERSES for cycling, where women are typically about half as likely to cycle as men; in high-cycling cities the two genders are equally likely, and in Berlin, Munich and Hamburg women cycle more than men. The gap is age-dependent: among children under 16 the metrics are often equal, and the disparity widens with age. On age itself, older travellers drive, walk and take taxis and make little use of bicycles or rideshare, car use falls and dependence on transit rises as the ability to drive falls, and older women are the group most likely to use public transport; an urban Italian study puts men at ~1.5x the odds of choosing a private car over an active mode. No Australian mode-choice model published an age or sex coefficient this pass could read.https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614415/2026-09-07

E20ELight rail: tram priority, dwellINDwell A.lightrail.dwell_fixed_s 8 + charging dwell per scenario (cities/newcastle/build/build_charging_dwell_offsets.py:152), capacity 270/60/210, disclosed boardings target 2,954/weekday; tram priority BUILT (TramPriorityController.java:73, :381 green extension) and OFF in S2 by design (A.lightrail.tsp_enabled false = the S2b intervention); signals and crossings re-derived on the footpath network (54 approaches).light_rail -58.6 and moving AWAY: supply exonerated (252 departures), the corridor market present; the missing control is the router's (F5).Transit signal priority produces large, repeatedly measured delay reductions for the priority vehicle and small costs to cross traffic: 53% and 43% reductions in average bus delay at two studied intersections against 14% and 16% increases in major-phase delay, and in Toronto TSP reduced transit delay 30-40% and travel time 2-6%. Dwell follows the TCQSM linear form - a base plus per-boarding and per-alighting service times; one calibrated model gives a 5.14 s base, 3.48 s per boarding and 1.70 s per alighting, with TCQSM service times of 4.5 s (exact change), 2 s (visual inspection) and 1.75 s (no fare payment).https://www.itskrs.its.dot.gov/2019-b013622026-09-07

E24EFreight trainINCHANGED. Freight rail is deliberately not a mobsim vehicle (9.70: the coal chain is grade-separated); its road effect is time-variant closures at two crossings (A.crossings.representation change_events, closure_source schedule_derived). A.crossings.freight_closures_per_day is now DERIVED per site - {Saint James Road 44, Clyde Street 48}, sweep [30, 70] - from the Cobbora Coal Project EA ch. 13 March 2012 five-day survey (1592f5b, 9.167, #184), with closure durations from the same survey (A.crossings.closure_duration_s 277 s freight, closure_duration_passenger_s 160 s; both literature now), emitted by cities/newcastle/build/build_level_crossings.py:76/:84/:105/:477 and counted by build_mode_targets.py:791-823: 405 closures a weekday (110 + 203 scheduled, 44 + 48 freight). The previous pass's PARTIAL rested on the assumed 0 that press evidence contradicted; both are superseded.freight_train representation-only (405 closures = timetable + survey); the closure effect on road traffic has never been measured on a converged arm, and F35 arm 0 is the first arm to carry the derived closures.The road-side effect of a freight train is the level-crossing closure, and its length is set by warning-time design as much as by the train: at investigated Australian crossings warning times could be cut by 10-40 s per activation, freight trains run below line speed and so hold the boom longer than passenger trains, and closures at peak produce queue spillback into adjacent signalised intersections; a Brisbane simulation study of seven problem crossings tested treatments on exactly these delays.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2213624X203004072026-09-07
F1FRoute choice and re-routingINReRoute 0.15 in RUN.replanning.weights (RUN_execution.json:330), RUN.routing.routing_randomness 3.0 (:1494), travel-time bins; router and mobsim read one gradient/bike-stress cost (GradientLinkSpeed.Router CitysimControler.java:393; BikeStressDisutility :410); RUN.travel_time.filter_modes true since F31.counts +16.3 % mean / -1.1 % median on the repaired station map: route choice is not what the board is short of.Route choice is estimated on GPS-observed routes with path-size logit corrections for overlapping paths, and the observed share taking the shortest path is small: over 25,157 trips by 143 subjects tracked for 8-13 weeks in Minneapolis-St Paul, 34% of all trips exactly matched the shortest-travel-time path and 40% matched within a 10% tolerance, while for commute trips alone the figures were 13.5% and 21.7%; no subject followed a shortest-DISTANCE path unless it coincided with the shortest-time one. About 50% of trips were within 30 s and about 90% within 5 minutes of the shortest-time route, so the deviation is wide in route space and narrow in time. A Chongqing trajectory study of 2,860 private-car trips by ~400 drivers puts the shortest-path match at ~67% under a looser matching rule. In iterative agent simulation the route set is co-evolved rather than enumerated.https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.01343222026-09-07
F2FParking search and occupancyPARTIALSearch time is charged as a derived scoring cost (A.parking.search_time_representation scoring, A_supply.json:1621; A.parking.search_min_max 8.1 min :1641 x density weight; build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1031-1040); A.parking.capacity_default and occupancy_profile are consumed by build_landuse_parking.py only - no run-time occupancy or search on the network.car +11.3: the CBD car trip pays a fixed minutes penalty whatever the lot is doing; a live occupancy would only bind in the 150 priced zones.Cruising for parking is a measured, large phenomenon: 3.5-14 minutes to find a curb space in congested downtowns, 8-74% of the traffic stream cruising (over 70% in recent work), and search time up to 40% of total travel time. A price that holds roughly one vacancy in eight removes the incentive to cruise and drives search time to zero.http://shoup.bol.ucla.edu/Cruising.pdf2026-09-07
F3FBoarding, denied boarding and crowdingINCapacity binds physically (transitVehicles patched from published seats/standing, build_matsim_run_inputs.py:380-383) with RUN.sample.transit_capacity_scaling true at a floor (run_matsim.py:297, :320); crowding disutility (E11) live.heavy_rail +225.0 with only standing load priced (seated multiplier 1.0 = off).Denied boarding and in-vehicle crowding are the same evidence base: Wardman and Whelan's 208 valuations give a seated multiplier of 1.19 and a standing multiplier of 2.32, i.e. a minute standing in a crowded vehicle costs more than twice a minute seated in an empty one, and the standing multiplier is of the same order as walk and wait multipliers.https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01441647.2010.5191272026-09-07
F4FRide pairing / matchingINRidePairingEngine pairs declared and inferred legs (B.ride.pairing_rule both_links, window 15/60 min), pair rate 0.9965 at the F28 gate; ride_pairing.csv carries miss_declared_absent; RemodeRestore.restore (RemodeRestore.java:95) re-finds a walked leg by endpoints and since 4a375f4 the engine routes the fallback itself (644 in 0.9 s at 25 %).ride -41.0: pairing is solved (99.6 % of declared pairs realise both tours); the miss is the passenger's mode assignment, changed at the demand and unread.Two literatures answer this and they are not the same. On PLATFORMS, pooled matching is measured directly: New York taxi pooling reached a 13% match rate on an ordinary day with passengers accepting up to 400 s of delay for up to 49% cost saving; a Chengdu ride-pooling dataset reached 86.6% matching at a 0.12 detour ratio; driver detours of ~9.2 min are reported when riders are matched to drivers with nearby destinations. H5HLLM-driven agentsOUTNo LLM agent anywhere in src/ or the Java trees (grep 'llm|language model|openai|anthropic': none).None.Two 2025-2026 results now bracket this lane. On the optimistic side, GATSim integrates LLM-powered generative agents - hierarchical memory, multi-modal retrieval, planning, reactive and reflection processes, diverse socioeconomic profiles and lifelong learning - into an urban mobility environment, and reports validation at microscopic and macroscopic levels, claiming agents 'perform competitively with human annotators in role-playing scenarios' while 'naturally producing realistic macroscopic traffic patterns'; its abstract states no accuracy figure, no real city and no cost per agent-day. On the sceptical side, the first systematic evaluation against observed mobility (2026) measures AgentSociety and CitySim over Greater Paris (3,337 residents, 7 days) and Shanghai (58,502 users, 10 days) and separates 'face validity' from 'objective mobility realism': AgentSociety's travel-distance error is a Wasserstein distance of 14.83 plus or minus 0.35 km and CitySim's 7.53 plus or minus 1.67 km, with origin-destination similarity at a common-part-of-commuters of 0.138 plus or minus 0.018; trip-duration error is 24.41 plus or minus 0.24 minutes and dwell-time error 3.96 plus or minus 0.12 hours, against reference-sample variability of 0.29 minutes and 0.26 hours. Activity PROPORTIONS come out well (Jensen-Shannon divergence 0.0296) while activity SEQUENCES do not (0.1125), and mobility diversity is 'unstable across default prompting configurations'. The finding to carry: LLM agents reproduce qualitative mobility laws and aggregate activity mixes, and miss individual spatial behaviour by one to two orders of magnitude more than sampling error.https://arxiv.org/html/2606.138352026-09-08
H6HEquilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?PARTIALRelaxation is measured (src/analyse/summarise_run.py:139 relaxation; RUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp 0.5 read at :70, settle_margin_iterations :78) and the result run relaxed at 0.261 pp; no equilibrium GAP (opdyts/greedo) is computed; ride converged 190 iterations early while light rail moved away throughout.light_rail -58.6 moving AWAY across 300 iterations is a non-fixed-point reading the drift tolerance cannot see because the tram is 1,224 boardings on a 154,347-person sample.MATSim's mobsim/scoring/replanning loop is a Monte-Carlo co-evolutionary search, not a solved fixed point, and its own authors say so. Floetteroed's statement of the position is the clearest available: the assignment relies on approximate minimisation of an EQUILIBRIUM GAP measuring, for every agent, how much that agent could improve its score by changing its plan if all other agents kept theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium', and the method 'aims to reduce the gap in subsequent MATSim iterations, steering the simulation process towards a state that has a low gap, and hence may be deemed to be near an equilibrium point'. He names the reproducible computation of point equilibria as 'the single most important advantage' of the traditional four-step / static-assignment model - an advantage MATSim does not have by default - and supplies the emulation and greedo contribs that add gap minimisation to the loop, illustrated on a multimodal Greater Stockholm scenario with all-day route, departure-time and mode choice. The wider theory agrees: MATSim targets a STOCHASTIC user equilibrium (minimum PERCEIVED cost) rather than a Nash equilibrium; best-response dynamics carry no convergence guarantee, though if they converge they converge to an equilibrium. No published convergence rate exists for a multimodal MATSim scenario: relaxation is asserted by observation, not proved.https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/baug/ivt/ivt-dam/events/2023/09/05/abstracts/Floetteroed_MUM_2023.pdf2026-09-08
H7HIn-loop parameter estimation from a ground-truth subpopulationOUTNo in-loop estimation; C1 parameters are literature, the ASC step is a between-run contraction (I6).None.An architecture that avoids the outer loop entirely: estimate the utility parameters INSIDE the simulation, against a subpopulation of real survey respondents whose observed plans are pinned. The MATSim planParamCalibration extension does exactly that - a designated subpopulation carries its surveyed plan under the KeepLastSelected strategy so those plans are the ground truth, the remaining agents generate alternatives by the ordinary strategies, and CMA-ES maximises a logit-like log-likelihood over the planCalcScore parameters (mode constants, marginal utility of travelling, of distance and of money, daily monetary constants, typical and minimal activity durations, line-switch, waiting, late-arrival and early-departure terms) at each MATSim iteration, writing the result back into the config for the next one. It stops on a designated iteration or on convergence, the default being an average estimated difference below 0.001. Tested on a 2023 street-interview trip-diary survey plus mobile-location commuting arrays at 100 m grid accuracy, the maximum log-likelihood is stable over twenty MATSim iterations and essentially unchanged whether the calibration population is respondents alone or respondents plus 100k, 300k, 600k or one million commuting records - the claimed proof that the estimator is auto-adaptive to population scale. The price of the architecture is exactly the data an aggregate-only city lacks: the likelihood's observations are unit-record plans.https://www.matsim.org/conferences/mum2024/presentations/MUM2024_Lu.pdf2026-09-08

A utility-informed neural network trained on 14,671 trips from the 2017 US National Household Travel Survey for California reached 89.03% mode-choice accuracy, the highest in its benchmark against MNL and other classifiers; alternative-specific-utility deep networks (ASU-DNN) and residual-logit hybrids (ResLogit) are likewise consistently more accurate than MNL on the same data. The published caution is sharper than the accuracy claim: the models with the best DISAGGREGATE predictive performance - gradient-boosted trees and random forests - give POORER estimates of behavioural indicators and of AGGREGATE MODE SHARES than deep neural networks and than plain multinomial logit. Every method in this family is estimated on unit-record choice observations with the alternatives' attributes attached; none can be fitted to a published aggregate share table, and none has been shown to sit inside an equilibrium loop where the attributes of the alternatives are themselves simulation outputs.https://arxiv.org/html/1909.074812026-09-08
